data.narrative:
RoboTwin is a seed-stage robotics and manufacturing company founded by Megi Mejdrechová, Ladislav Dvořák, and David Polák. The company has raised €2.3M in EIC funding. The broader robotics and manufacturing sector comprises 1 public comparable (ticker 277810.KQ) and 8 private peers including Walden Robotics, Divergent, Exotec, Locus Robotics, and Generalist AI.

The valuation analysis relies on stage-progression methodology, as peer-median approaches proved inapplicable due to insufficient narrow-set comparables. The robotics sector contains 10 same-sector peers overall, but same-stage and adjacent-stage filtering yielded fewer than three datapoints needed for reliable peer benchmarking. Using the €2.3M total raised as a base proxy and applying a 2.5x step-up multiplier typical for seed-to-next-stage progression yields an implied valuation of $6M.

The analysis supports a valuation range of $5M to $7M, with a median estimate of $6M. This range reflects stage-appropriate step-up dynamics but carries material uncertainty stemming from the absence of sufficiently comparable peer valuations. Key risks to this estimate include limited publicly available pricing for early-stage robotics companies, sector-specific technical differentiation that may command premium or discount multiples, and macroeconomic factors affecting hardware-intensive venture rounds. A fuller peer set or evidence of customer traction would materially improve conviction in the final range.
